claim: Transport of solutes through brain involves diffusion and convection.
source: Transport of solutes through brain involves diffusion and convection.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: The importance of convective flow in the subarachnoid and paravascular spaces has long been recognized.
source: The importance of convective flow in the subarachnoid and paravascular spaces has long been recognized
evidence: This is presented as established scientific consensus.

claim: The glymphatic mechanism proposes that aquaporin-4 (AQP4) water channels facilitate convective transport through brain parenchyma.
source: a recently proposed 'glymphatic' clearance mechanism additionally suggests that aquaporin-4 (AQP4) water channels facilitate convective transport through brain parenchyma.
evidence: This is a description of a previously proposed hypothesis.

claim: Transport of fluorescent dextrans in brain parenchyma depended on dextran size in a manner consistent with diffusive rather than convective transport.
source: (i) transport of fluorescent dextrans in brain parenchyma depended on dextran size in a manner consistent with diffusive rather than convective transport
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: Transport of dextrans in the parenchymal extracellular space was not affected just after cardiorespiratory arrest.
source: (ii) transport of dextrans in the parenchymal extracellular space, measured by 2-photon fluorescence recovery after photobleaching, was not affected just after cardiorespiratory arrest
evidence: This is a primary finding from the photobleaching experiments.

claim: Aqp4 gene deletion did not impair transport of fluorescent solutes from subarachnoid space to brain in mice or rats.
source: (iii) Aqp4 gene deletion did not impair transport of fluorescent solutes from sub-arachnoid space to brain in mice or rats.
evidence: This is a primary finding from experiments comparing Aqp4+/+ and Aqp4-/- animals.

claim: The results do not support the proposed glymphatic mechanism of convective solute transport in brain parenchyma.
source: Our results do not support the proposed glymphatic mechanism of convective solute transport in brain parenchyma.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Solute movement through the narrow, tortuous ECS in brain parenchyma occurs by a diffusive mechanism.
source: The conventional paradigm, which is supported by a large body of experimental evidence, is that solute movement through the narrow, tortuous ECS in brain parenchyma occurs by a diffusive mechanism, whose determinants include solute size and physical properties, and ECS structure and composition (Syková and Nicholson, 2008; Verkman, 2013).
evidence: This is presented as established scientific consensus supported by citations.

claim: Nedergaard and colleagues proposed that convective, 'glymphatic' flow of cerebrospinal fluid though the ECS from the para-arterial to the para-venous spaces is largely responsible for solute transport in parenchymal ECS.
source: More recently, Nedergaard and colleagues (Iliff et al., 2012; Jessen et al., 2015) have proposed that convective, 'glymphatic' flow of cerebrospinal fluid though the ECS from the para-arterial to the para-venous spaces is largely responsible for solute transport in parenchymal ECS.
evidence: This is a description of a previously proposed hypothesis with citations.

claim: Glymphatic transport was proposed to have broad consequences in normal brain physiology and in the diseased brain, including clearance of β-amyloid in neurodegenerative disease.
source: Glymphatic transport was proposed to have broad consequences in normal brain physiology and in the diseased brain, including clearance of β-amyloid in neurodegenerative disease (Iliff et al., 2012)
evidence: This is a description of a previously proposed hypothesis with citation.

claim: Glymphatic transport was proposed to facilitate removal of metabolic waste products during sleep.
source: Glymphatic transport was proposed to have broad consequences in normal brain physiology and in the diseased brain, including clearance of β-amyloid in neurodegenerative disease (Iliff et al., 2012) and metabolic waste products during sleep (Xie et al., 2013)
evidence: This is a description of a previously proposed hypothesis with citation.

claim: Glymphatic transport was proposed to facilitate removal of excess fluid in various forms of brain edema.
source: Glymphatic transport was proposed to have broad consequences in normal brain physiology and in the diseased brain, including clearance of β-amyloid in neurodegenerative disease (Iliff et al., 2012) and metabolic waste products during sleep (Xie et al., 2013), and removal of excess fluid in various forms of brain edema (Thrane et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a description of a previously proposed hypothesis with citation.

claim: It was proposed that AQP4 facilitates convective solute transport.
source: It was further proposed that AQP4, a water channel expressed on astrocyte endfeet, facilitates convective solute transport (Iliff et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a description of a previously proposed hypothesis with citation.

claim: The glymphatic mechanism and a role for AQP4 have been questioned based on apparent inconsistencies with prior data on solute transport in brain ECS.
source: The glymphatic mechanism and a role for AQP4 have been questioned based on apparent inconsistencies with prior data on solute transport in brain ECS (Hladky and Barrand, 2014; Spector et al., 2015)
evidence: This is a description of previous critiques with citations.

claim: The plausibility of convective, pressure-driven fluid flow from para-arterial to para-venous spaces through parenchymal ECS is uncertain.
source: as well as the uncertain plausibility of convective, pressure-driven fluid flow from para-arterial to para-venous spaces through parenchymal ECS (Asgari et al., 2016; Asgari et al., 2015; Jin et al., 2016; Smith et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a description of previous critiques with citations.

claim: Diffusive transport depends strongly on solute size (hydrodynamic radius, Rh).
source: Diffusive transport depends strongly on solute size (hydrodynamic radius, Rh)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about diffusion.

claim: Convective transport of uncharged solutes through a porous medium is approximately independent of solute size if the ratio of solute size to pore size is less than ~0.5.
source: whereas convective transport of uncharged solutes through a porous medium is approximately independent of solute size if the ratio of solute size to pore size is less than ~0.5 (Dechadilok and Deen, 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: 10, 70 and 2000 kDa dextrans have hydrodynamic radii of approximately 2, 5 and 12 nm respectively.
source: fluorescently labeled, fixable dextrans (10, 70 and 2000 kDa) with different diffusional mobilities (Rh of approximately 2, 5 and 12 nm [Hadjiev and Amsden, 2015])
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the values.

claim: All three dextrans (10, 70 and 2000 kDa) were seen at the brain surface and in the paravascular spaces after fixation at 60 min following cisternal injection.
source: All three dextrans were seen at the brain surface and in the paravascular spaces after fixation (Figure 1A)

evidence: This is a conclusion from modeling compared to experimental data.

claim: Absolute penetration distances were not predicted accurately by the diffusion model.
source: However, absolute penetration distances were not predicted accurately by the model
evidence: This is an observation from comparing model predictions to experimental data.

claim: Additional factors, such as solute clearance or barriers between the subarachnoid and subpial spaces, may affect the extent of solute penetration in vivo.
source: probably because additional factors, such as solute clearance or barriers between the subarachnoid and subpial spaces, also affect the extent of solute penetration in vivo.

source: At early times points the distribution of all three dextrans was similar (Figure 2A)

claim: Similar convection of all three dextrans into the brain occurred during the pressure pulses applied to the injection pipette.
source: suggesting similar convection into the brain during the pressure pulses applied to the injection pipette.

claim: Dextran penetration from the injection site into the surrounding parenchyma at 60 min was strongly size-dependent.
source: However, dextran penetration from the injection site into the surrounding parenchyma at 60 min was strongly size-dependent (Figure 2A,B).

source: and support the long-standing idea that paravascular spaces act as a low resistance pathway for convective clearance of solutes from the brain.

claim: The role of arterial pulsation in moving CSF in the subarachnoid and paravascular spaces is well-established.
source: Although the role of arterial pulsation in moving CSF in the subarachnoid and paravascular spaces is well-established (Rennels et al., 1990)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: It had not been previously suggested that arterial pulsation could drive fluid flow through the interstitial space.
source: it had not been previously been suggested that arterial pulsation could drive fluid flow through the interstitial space.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the glymphatic hypothesis.

claim: Solute transport was unaltered in the period immediately following cardiac arrest.
source: We directly assessed the contribution of arterial pulsatility to solute movement in the interstitial space by photobleaching of 150 kDa FITC-dextran and found that solute transport was unaltered in the period immediately following cardiac arrest.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: The substantial reduction in solute transport following anoxic depolarization at 4 min after cardiorespiratory arrest is consistent with previous reports of astrocyte swelling.
source: The substantial reduction in solute transport following anoxic depolarization seen at 4 min after cardiorespiratory arrest is consistent with previous reports of astrocyte swelling (Risher et al., 2009)
evidence: This is a comparison to prior work with citation.

claim: The substantial reduction in solute transport following anoxic depolarization is consistent with hindered extracellular space diffusion due to increased tortuosity.
source: and hindered extracellular space diffusion due to increased tortuosity (Zoremba et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior work with citation.

claim: The reduction in parenchymal tracer accumulation observed by Iliff et al. is likely due to factors other than inhibition of pulsatile flow through the interstitial space.
source: We conclude that the reduction in parenchymal tracer accumulation observed by Iliff et al. (Iliff et al., 2013) is likely due to factors other than inhibition of pulsatile flow through the interstitial space
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Reduction in ECS volume due to partial ischemia may explain the reduction in parenchymal tracer accumulation observed by Iliff et al.
source: such as reduction in ECS volume due to partial ischemia (Syková et al., 1994)
evidence: This is speculation about alternative explanations with citation.

claim: Inhibition of fluid movement in the paravascular space may explain the reduction in parenchymal tracer accumulation observed by Iliff et al.
source: or inhibition of fluid movement in the paravascular space.
evidence: This is speculation about alternative explanations.

claim: Aqp4 deletion in mice or rats did not reduce the transfer of solutes into brain parenchyma following intracisternal injection.
source: The glymphatic mechanism proposes glial involvement in solute transport facilitated by AQP4; however, we found that Aqp4 deletion in mice or rats did not reduce, but perhaps slightly increased, the transfer of solutes into brain parenchyma following intracisternal injection.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: A small increase in parenchymal macromolecular diffusion in Aqp4-/- mice was previously found.
source: A small increase in parenchymal macromolecular diffusion in Aqp4-/- mice was previously found (Binder et al., 2004)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: The small increase in parenchymal macromolecular diffusion in Aqp4-/- mice is probably due to an expanded ECS.
source: which is probably due to an expanded ECS (Yao et al., 2008; Zhang and Verkman, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as an explanation with citations.

claim: The mildly greater solute diffusion in Aqp4-/- than in Aqp4+/+ mouse brain could account for the results.
source: The mildly greater solute diffusion in Aqp4-/- than in Aqp4+/+ mouse brain could account for the results here.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The difference between the results and the earlier report of Iliff et al. may be due to differences in experimental methodology or data analysis.
source: The difference between the results here and the earlier report of Iliff et al. (Iliff et al., 2012) may be due to differences in experimental methodology or data analysis.
evidence: This is speculation about the source of discrepancies.

claim: Beveled glass micropipettes of ~40 μm diameter and pulsed pressure injection were used in this study.
source: For example, beveled glass micropipettes of ~40 μm diameter and pulsed pressure injection were used here
evidence: This is a description of the methods used.

claim: Iliff et al. used a 30-gauge metal syringe and constant flow injection for solute application into the cisterna magna.
source: whereas Iliff et al. used a 30-gauge metal syringe and constant flow injection for solute application into the cisterna magna.
evidence: This is a description of the methods used in prior work.

claim: The choice of anesthetics may have differed between the two sets of experiments.
source: The choice of anesthetics may have also differed between the two sets of experiments (avertin vs. unspecified).
evidence: This is speculation about potential methodological differences.

claim: The analysis method used by Iliff et al. is inherently non-quantitative as it is based on subjective intensity thresholding.
source: The analysis method used by Iliff et al., and reproduced here in Figure 5B for comparison purposes, is inherently non-quantitative as it is based on subjective intensity thresholding that treats large differences in fluorescence intensity, indicative of large variation in solute concentration, as equal.
evidence: This is a critique of the analysis method.

claim: The experiments and their analyses were done by an investigator blinded to genotype information.
source: Finally, the experiments and their analyses here were done by an investigator blinded to genotype information.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: The results do not support a role for AQP4 in convection-driven clearance of beta amyloid.
source: Our results also do not support a role for AQP4 in convection-driven clearance of beta amyloid
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: The results do not rule out the possibility that AQP4 may contribute to the pathology of Alzheimer's disease in other ways.
source: though they do not rule out the possibility that AQP4 may contribute to the pathology of Alzheimer's disease in other ways.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the conclusions.

claim: Aqp4+/+ or Aqp4-/- mice on a CD1 background of either sex at 3–6 months of age were used for experiments.
source: Aqp4+/+ or Aqp4-/- mice on a CD1 background (Ma et al., 1997) of either sex at 3–6 months of age were used for experiments.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental subjects.

claim: Aqp4-/- rats were generated using CRISPR-Cas9 technology.
source: Aqp4-/- rats were generated using CRISPR-Cas9 technology, which will be reported separately.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental subjects.

claim: All experiments were approved by the UCSF Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
source: All experiments were approved by the UCSF Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
evidence: This is a statement about ethical approval.
